officialTitle: Sunitinib in patients with chemotherapy-refractory thymoma and thymic carcinoma: an open-label phase 2 trial
setting: Thymic epithelial tumours progressing after platinum-based chemotherapy

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: 41 patients were enrolled, 25 with thymic carcinoma and 16 with thymoma.
primaryEndpoints: Best tumour response (investigator-assessed), by histology cohort
design.notes: Single-arm open-label phase 2 trial with separate thymic carcinoma and thymoma cohorts. Non-comparative evidence.

sponsor: National Cancer Institute (Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program)
clinicalQuestion: Is sunitinib active in thymic epithelial tumours refractory to platinum-based chemotherapy?

pico.population: Thymic carcinoma or thymoma progressing after at least one platinum-containing regimen, ECOG PS 2 or lower
pico.intervention: Sunitinib 50 mg daily, 4 weeks on / 2 weeks off

arms.label: Thymic carcinoma cohort
arms.dosing: 50 mg orally once daily, 4 weeks on followed by 2 weeks off (6-week cycles)
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients received 50 mg of sunitinib orally once a day, in 6-week cycles (ie, 4 weeks of treatment followed by 2 weeks without treatment), until tumour progression or unacceptable toxic effects arose.

arms.label: Thymoma cohort
arms.dosing: 50 mg orally once daily, 4 weeks on followed by 2 weeks off (6-week cycles)
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients received 50 mg of sunitinib orally once a day, in 6-week cycles (ie, 4 weeks of treatment followed by 2 weeks without treatment), until tumour progression or unacceptable toxic effects arose.

publications.title: Sunitinib in patients with chemotherapy-refractory thymoma and thymic carcinoma: an open-label phase 2 trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Of 23 assessable patients with thymic carcinoma, six (26%, 90% CI 12.1-45.3, 95% CI 10.2-48.4) had partial responses, 15 (65%, 95% CI 42.7-83.6) achieved stable disease, and two (9%, 1.1-28.0) had progressive disease.
Of 16 patients with thymoma, one (6%, 95% CI 0.2-30.2) had a partial response, 12 (75%, 47.6-92.7) had stable disease, and three (19%, 4.1-45.7) had progressive disease.

safety.description: Grade 3-4 treatment-related lymphocytopenia, fatigue and oral mucositis (each)
safety.sourceQuote: The most common grade 3 and 4 treatment-related adverse events were lymphocytopenia (eight [20%] of 40 patients), fatigue (eight [20%]), and oral mucositis (eight [20%]).

safety.description: Decrease in left-ventricular ejection fraction (grade 3 in three patients)
safety.sourceQuote: Five (13%) patients had decreases in left-ventricular ejection fraction, of which three (8%) were grade 3 events.

safety.description: Deaths during treatment, one cardiac arrest possibly treatment-related
safety.sourceQuote: Three (8%) patients died during treatment, including one individual who died of cardiac arrest that was possibly treatment-related.

strengths: Prospective trial with prespecified histology-specific cohorts
Addresses a population with no established standard after platinum failure
limitations: Single-arm phase II evidence with small cohorts; no comparator
Cardiac toxicity signal (reduced ejection fraction) requires monitoring

clinicalImplications.text: Single-arm phase II data showing activity of sunitinib in platinum-refractory thymic carcinoma, with minimal activity in thymoma; cardiac function monitoring is warranted.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Antiangiogenic TKIs appear more active in thymic carcinoma than thymoma; check baseline ejection fraction before sunitinib.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 25592632.
